You don\'t need to turn on \'Shortcut\'.\n\nBourget uses the accessibility service to show a confirmation popup, or open another app you chose in advance, when an app or website you picked is opened. When the screen changes, it checks the package name of the app in front, and in supported browsers (Chrome, Samsung Internet) it reads only the address shown in the address bar to compare it with your website rules. It does not read anything else on screen, such as page content. The app names, addresses and browsing history it checks are never stored or sent anywhere. Only the app and website rules and popup text you create are stored on this device, and they are backed up to your Google account through Android backup only if you turn backup on in settings. Bourget has no internet permission.
When an app or website you picked is opened, Bourget shows a confirmation popup or opens another app you chose in advance.
To do this, the accessibility service checks:\n• Which app is on screen now\n• The address shown in a browser\'s address bar

• It does not read anything on screen other than the address bar, such as page content or what you type.\n• It does not store app usage or browsing history. Only the app and website rules you create are stored on this device, and they are backed up to your Google account only if you turn backup on in settings.\n• Bourget has no internet permission, so it never sends any information off the device itself. Only a backup you turn on is sent to your Google account, by the Android system.
You can turn the service off in settings at any time.
One must live the way one thinks, or end up thinking the way one has lived.

Bourget helps you pause and think before an app or website you open out of habit, by showing a confirmation popup or opening another app instead.\n\nIt is not meant to block apps: you can always choose to keep using them.

Effective date: November 22, 2026

1. Information checked
Bourget uses the accessibility service to check only the following.
• The package name of the app in front when the screen changes: used to compare it with the app rules you made.
• The address shown in the address bar of supported browsers (Chrome, Samsung Internet): only its domain is used, to compare it with the websites you added.
What is checked is used only for this comparison and is discarded right away, never stored. Nothing else on screen, such as page content or what you type, is read. Nothing is checked before you agree to this notice.
When a rule matches, Bourget shows a confirmation popup or opens another app you chose for the rule. Opening another app checks or stores nothing more. The counts for today shown in the popup (how many times the popup appeared and how many times you continued, per rule) are kept only in memory while the service is on, never written to a file, and disappear when the day changes or the service is turned off.

2. Information stored
• App rules you made: the app's package name, whether it is on, its action (popup or opening another app), and the package name of the app to open
• Website rules you added: the domain, whether it is on, its action, and the package name of the app to open
• The popup text you set
• Whether you have seen the intro, whether backup is on, and the version of this notice you agreed to
• The app language you chose (on Android 12 and below only; on Android 13 and above the Android system keeps it)
By default this information is stored only on this device. App usage and browsing history are not stored.

3. Backup (optional)
Only if you turn on "Back up to Google account" in settings does Android backup save the information above to your Google account. Backups are made only when they can be encrypted on a device with a screen lock, and they are sent by the Android system, not by Bourget. When you set up a new device with the same account, your rules and popup text move over; your consent does not, so you agree again on the new device. Backup is off by default.

4. Transfer and sharing
Bourget has no internet permission, so it never sends any information off the device or shares it with third parties itself. The only thing stored off the device is the Android backup you turn on. Bourget uses no advertising, analytics or crash reporting tools. Tapping "Source code" in settings opens the source code page in your device's browser.

5. Retention and deletion
Stored information is deleted when you delete a rule, clear the app's data, or uninstall the app. After you turn backup off, later backups no longer include Bourget's information, and backups left in your Google account can be deleted in the device's Google backup settings. Rules for uninstalled apps are cleaned up when you open Bourget, and rules whose app to open was uninstalled switch to the popup.

6. Your choices
If you don't agree, Bourget checks nothing. You can turn the accessibility service off in device settings at any time. You can turn backup on and off in Bourget's settings.

7. Changes
If the information checked or stored changes, the app tells you again and asks for your agreement.
